out.other_title: Easy-to-hard results limited to tasks with reliable human labels
out.rationale: Hase et al. state their easy-to-hard results are limited to tasks humans label reliably and may not hold where humans cannot produce accurate labels. Wen et al. report a task where 5 human annotators are consistent but only 60% accurate while ICM matches golden labels at 80%; evaluation still uses golden labels, so the test setting itself has ground truth.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether capabilities can be elicited on tasks where human labels are unreliable, for author-gender prediction where humans reach 60%

open_obligations: Check whether ICM gives any justification for its labels that a judge could verify; the cited passage reports only label accuracy.

out.other_title: Can debate extract inductive or tacit knowledge that lacks short, citeable justifications?
out.rationale: Michael et al. note inductive or tacit knowledge may not admit short justifications and that alternative extraction methods may be needed. Wen et al. report ICM elicits a pretrained model's author-gender prediction at 80% (matching golden labels) while human labels reach only 60%; this is unsupervised label elicitation, not debate, and correctness is checked with golden labels. No cited passage shows author-gender prediction to be knowledge that lacks short justifications, so Wen et al.'s result does not bear on Michael et al.'s question, and Michael et al.'s question does not bear on Wen et al.'s result.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: methods for extracting knowledge or capabilities from AI models, in Michael et al.'s suggestion that alternative extraction methods may be needed for knowledge that may not admit short justifications and in Wen et al.'s unsupervised elicitation of a pretrained model's author-gender prediction

text: The paper reports that on author gender prediction from pairs of blog posts, human labels from 5 annotators are perfectly consistent but inaccurate (60% on the test set, 53.8% on the training set), while ICM matches golden supervision at 80% accuracy. Prompting with weak human labels or commercial post-training fails to fully use the pretrained model's superhuman capability.
title: ICM elicits superhuman author-gender prediction: 80% vs 60% for human labels
